featured_reviews.name: Vipul J Meher
featured_reviews.review_text:
My experience at this shop was very disappointing. I bought a pair of JoyBean brand sandals for ₹1,500. The shopkeeper initially quoted ₹1,900, and after bargaining, I purchased them for ₹1,500. However, when I returned home and checked the brand’s official website, I found that the MRP was ₹1,399 and the selling price was ₹1,245. Moreover, the original price tag had been removed from the item.

It appears that inflating the price first and then reducing it during bargaining is a tactic used to make customers feel satisfied, while still giving the shopkeeper an unfair advantage.

This practice is misleading and unfair. I advise others to avoid such fraudulent shops. If you do visit, make sure to check the price tag and do not fall for the shopkeeper’s sweet talk.

featured_reviews.name: Sudhir Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
Outstanding service! After searching for size 11 sandals for three years and being turned away by dozens of bata stores, I finally found success here.
​Mr. Mangesh (Store Assistant) and Mr. Shyam (Store Manager) were incredibly helpful. Mr. Mangesh went above and beyond, sourcing my size from another branch overnight and ensuring I got a great discount. Their perseverance and customer-first attitude are rare to find. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Estel Ferrao
featured_reviews.review_text:
Walked into Bata expecting a basic retail experience. Apparently, that expectation was premium.

The sales staff were completely unhelpful. I asked a simple question… the difference between two products of the same brand. Instead of clarity, I got confusion. No product knowledge. No effort to check. No attempt to assist. Just blank expressions and vague replies. If you’re selling the product, shouldn’t you at least know what you’re selling?

And then came the highlight.

After paying ₹7,000 for a pair of shoes, they packed it in a jute bag. No shoe box. Nothing. For a ₹7k purchase. That’s a bold interpretation of “customer experience.”
When I pointed it out, they disappeared and returned with a random, battered shoe box that looked like it had been through several clearance sales and maybe a flood or two. That was the solution.

It’s not about the box. It’s about the attitude. Zero professionalism. Zero ownership. Zero pride.

For a brand that markets itself as reliable and established, this was genuinely disappointing.

“Surprisingly Bata”
